title: Rennes and PSG: Ligue 1 fairness crisis
seoTitle: Rennes and PSG: Ligue 1 Fairness Controversy
subtitle: Luis Enrique demands return leg be played at Parc des Princes
excerpt: The venue change for the first match between Rennes and PSG has sparked a debate over equal opportunities in Ligue 1.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The clash between Rennes and Paris Saint-Germain in matchday two of Ligue 1 became the center of attention when the first fixture, originally scheduled for the French capital, was moved to Roazhon Park in Rennes. The change occurred due to adverse pitch conditions at the Parc des Princes, worsened by heatwaves that damaged the turf. The situation raised questions about equal opportunities among the clubs.

Luis Enrique's reaction

In a press conference, Luis Enrique made it clear that PSG must host Rennes at the Parc des Princes in the return fixture. He cited the principle of equality, stating that “you cannot play twice away from home against the same team. All clubs must play once away and once at home.” The manager did not refer to specific regulations, but stressed that the move to Rennes was an exceptional circumstance.

Role of French league rules

PSG argues that the venue change falls under what the French Football Federation describes as “exceptional circumstances,” in accordance with Article 501.3 of the league regulations. So far, Ligue 1 has not announced a decision regarding the possibility of reversing the fixture order.

Impact on Rennes' schedule

According to media reports, Rennes does not want to give up its right to play the second match at its home stadium. If the return leg is kept at the Parc des Princes, the club will only host one match in the season, which, according to Enrique, would be unfair, as the switch for the first match was driven by factors outside sporting control.

PSG squad for the clash

For the match, PSG will feature the first call-ups for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, both recent transfers. The squad includes Safonov, Chevalier, Longoni, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Digne, L. Hernandez, Vitinha, Joao Neves, Fabian Ruiz, Zaïre-Emery, Dro Fernandez, Beraldo, Dembélé, Kvaratshkelia, Doué, Ferran Torres, Godts, and Akliouche. Absentees include Senny Mayulu, Bradley Barcola, Ibrahim Mbaye, and Nuno Mendes, who is serving a three-match suspension.

Next steps

The final decision on the fixture order still awaits the French league. Meanwhile, the debate continues regarding the need to ensure fair playing conditions for all clubs involved in the competition.

With information from Goal.com, OneFootball.
